newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Yavlinsky calls NATO growth a dangerous diversion.
newsitem.headline: Yavlinsky calls NATO growth a dangerous diversion.

text.p: Russian liberal opposition leader Grigory Yavlinsky warned on Monday that eastward expansion of NATO could harm democracy in Russia and divert European attention from new threats to security.

Yavlinsky, who heads the reformist Yabloko faction in the Russian State Duma lower house of parliament, said he did not view the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation as a threat but that expansion could hurt the reformist cause in Russia.
"The expansion of NATO as an internal issue is a bad issue for us. It would create tendencies in Russian internal politics which I consider bad for Russian democracy," he said.
The Yabloko leader told a conference that NATO expansion could boost the military-industrial complex in Russia and that anti-Western sentiment would be more easy to exploit.

NATO expansion could divert European attention from what he said were the new and more real threats to European security such as terrorism, the control of the former Soviet Union's stockpiles of chemical, biological and nuclear weapons, and ecological problems.
But Yavlinsky reserved some of his most scathing comments for NATO as an institution which he said was essentially redundant and needed expansion to justify its existence.
"Big bureacratic structures are always looking for something to do if they have nothing to do. So the best thing for bureacratic structures is expansion," he said.

He also questioned the motives of Western powers in offering NATO membership to former east bloc countries, saying European Union countries were afraid of low cost competition from post-communist countries.
"I think that to some extent NATO expansion is a replacement for the issue of taking Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary into the economic union of Europe."
Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are expected to start negotiations on NATO membership after the summer. Moscow is fiercely opposed to any such move.
